context.why: Everything in this feature so far is invisible to a visitor. Somebody looking at a research portal for the first time wants to know who is behind it: who is in charge, who looks after the data, who to talk to about an account, and who built the thing. This story is the page that tells them, and it is the only part of this work anybody outside the team ever sees. It is also what gives the Developer role its purpose - that role holds no rights at all and exists so the people who build a portal are named on its team and credited for it.
spec_sections: User Story 5 - A visitor can see who runs the portal
Requirements / The portal team page (FR-030 to FR-035)
plan_sections: Phases / Phase 5 - US-5, the portal team page
prior_decisions: D18 - the page lists ACTIVE holders only. A deactivated account holds nothing, and naming a departed volunteer as the portal's administrator tells a visitor something untrue. FR-030 says so.
D1 - the Developer role holds no rights and exists for this page. It appears on it like any other role.

The page shows portal roles, never contribution roles. Those are credit on a record and have nothing to do with running the portal - CONTEXT.md keeps the two terms apart and this page is the easiest place to blur them.

PortalRoles.ROLES is the declaration order and the order the page presents. PortalRoles.shipped_names() and the role objects are the one source; never hard-code the four names or their order in a view or a template.
A role nobody holds is left off the page rather than shown empty (FR-034).

acceptance.given_when_then: Given people holding portal roles, When a visitor who is not signed in opens the page, Then 200, each role appears with the active people holding it in declaration order, somebody holding two roles appears under both, a role nobody holds is absent, a deactivated holder is absent, no email address appears anywhere in the response, and no contribution role appears. The page also holds its query count as the number of holders grows.
Given the route, When it is reached, Then it lives in fairdm/contrib/contributors beside people-list and organization-list, and each person is shown by name with a link to their public profile.
Given the main navigation, When a visitor opens the Community group, Then the portal team page is there beside People and Organizations, with an icon from the existing set.
Given an administrator reading the documentation, When they look up the team page, Then they find what it shows and that putting somebody in a role is what puts them on it.
